title: Presence and attention
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Can you be fully where you are for ten minutes?

I said that when you travel for the first time there is a purity and simplicity, because you are paying attention to the senses. Everything around you normally fights for your attention and pulls it to work in a particular way.
I said that when you are present and the usual stimulus is gone, your attention can seize opportunity, because your subconscious is maximized and your conscious mind concentrates.
I asked for a strategy. A student said: tune into the moment, meditate, appreciate. I said that in meditation you are making the subconscious conscious.

The student explained: set the intention to put your attention on a meditation object, typically the breath. Like driving on a highway, your brain picks up more than the car in front. Thoughts will pull your attention away.
I said: when you lose it, notice quickly and bring yourself back. You know you are getting better when you keep attention longer, and when you notice faster.

I said that repetition is probably the most effective strategy: you can beat yourself up over the money you should have made, or say: I have been successful in this situation before, I have felt this stress before. I will turn it in a positive direction and go into possibility thinking.
What would you do in a quiet ten minutes to bring yourself back?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what fights for your attention in a day.
Write one place or time with none of it.
Write your meditation object: breath, sound or a word.
Write how you will bring yourself back when you drift.
Write one past success you will repeat to yourself.

check.q: What did I say happens when you are present and free of stimulus?
What did a student say to do when you lose attention?
What did I say is probably the most effective strategy?

recap: Be present. Return to your object. Repeat the good.
